content: RBCK1, also known as RanBP-type and C3HC4-type zinc finger-containing protein 1, is a protein encoded by the RBCK1 gene in humans. This protein shares significant similarity with the mouse UIP28/UbcM4-interacting protein. The RBCK1 gene undergoes alternative splicing, which results in the production of distinct isoforms of the protein. Clinical Significance A previously unreported disease was identified in a family quartet, where two children presented with progressive muscular weakness and cardiomyopathy, while maintaining normal intelligence. During the course of the study, an additional unrelated patient was discovered with a similar clinical phenotype. Whole-genome sequencing identified RBCK1 as the most likely candidate gene responsible for the disease. RBCK1 encodes an E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase, and two protein-truncating mutations were identified in the probands of the first family. A 2 Mb copy-neutral region of homozygosity encompassing RBCK1 was also observed. RNA sequencing (RNA-Seq) confirmed aberrant splicing of RBCK1 transcripts, leading to the production of truncated protein products. Furthermore, ten additional individuals with mutations in RBCK1 and overlapping clinical phenotypes have been identified, further supporting the association of RBCK1 mutations with this disease.
